report.summary: Two product-level defects are active in the app under test: year_off_by_one lets a next-year publication year through, and leak_books makes GET /api/books return every user's books. Both are gated by the BUGS env var, which the repo's CI workflow does not set, so first find where BUGS=year_off_by_one,leak_books is coming from in this run's environment and unset it (or fix the two code paths). The four failures are otherwise deterministic and not test or infrastructure problems.

causes.title: GET /api/books returns other users' books (leak_books bug active)
causes.explanation: The API list endpoint returns every user's books instead of only the caller's. The API test sees another user's book id in the other user's list, and the new-user UI page renders books that belong to other users (the 'Final title' and 'From API' rows created by other tests). Because the new user's bookshelf is not empty, the empty-state element is not rendered. The leak is the root cause of both failures; the test assertions are correct.
evidence: tests/api/test_books_api.py:42: assert book["id"] not in other_ids  ->  E   assert 2 not in [1, 2]
app/main.py:163-164: if "leak_books" in BUGS: rows = conn.execute("SELECT * FROM books ORDER BY id").fetchall()
app/main.py:166: else: ... WHERE owner_id = ? (the correct, owner-filtered query is bypassed when the bug is on)
Aria snapshot for user-9a51ecb5 lists rows 'Final title Someone 2001' and 'From API-a09ceb99 Robot', which were created by other users' tests

app/templates/books.html:29-30: empty-state

is only rendered when {% if books %} is false
causes.suggested_fix: Restore the owner filter in list_books: always run the WHERE owner_id = ? query and remove the leak_books branch or ensure BUGS is empty in the test environment. Then rerun both tests.

causes.title: Validation accepts next year as a publication year (year_off_by_one bug active)
causes.explanation: validate_book allows years up to this_year+1 when the year_off_by_one bug flag is set, so a book dated next year is created with 201 and no error. The API test expects 422 and the UI test expects an error message and no row; both see the book saved. The tests are correct about the intended rule (the error message says 'between 1 and <this year>').
evidence: app/main.py:94: max_year = this_year + 1 if "year_off_by_one" in BUGS else this_year
app/main.py:95-96: if not 1 <= book.year <= max_year: raise HTTPException(422, f"Year must be between 1 and {this_year}")
tests/ui/test_books_ui.py:44: expect(books.error).to_contain_text("Year must be between")  ->  element(s) not found
Aria snapshot shows row 'Future-c4341a62 Someone 2027 Delete' was saved, so no error element was rendered
causes.suggested_fix: Remove the year_off_by_one branch so max_year is this_year, or make sure BUGS is not set in the test environment. Then rerun both year tests.
